newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Amsterdam port area traffic at new record in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Amsterdam port area traffic at new record in 1996.

text.p: Amsterdam area port traffic rose to a record 54.7 million tonnes in 1996, 8.8 percent higher than the total in 1995, the port authority said on Monday.

Shipments of dry bulk rose 4.8 percent to 35.4 million tonnes, with coal up 24.5 percent to 11.5 million tonnes and agri-bulk up 14.6 percent to 8.6 million tonnes. A downturn in the European steel sector last year caused a 16.3 percent fall in ore traffic to nine million tonnes, it said.
The port handled around 11 million tonnes of liquid bulk, up 13 percent on 1995. Oil products were up 16.2 percent to 8.3 million tonnes.

The general cargo sector rose 22.5 percent to 8.2 million tonnes with container shipping rising 55 percent to 1.7 million tonnes, reflecting increased traffic between Amsterdam and West Africa and South America.
The ro-ro sector continued its decline, dropping 21.3 percent to 500,000 tonnes.
The figures cover transhipments handled by the ports of Velsen, Beverwijk, Zaanstad and Amsterdam.
Last month, the country's biggest port, Rotterdam, announced a 0.5 percent fall in turnover in 1996 to 292 million tonnes.
